```{r setup}
library(rxs2tria)
```

## Overview

A `QWAimages` object is a tibble subclass — one row per analysed image —
that collects everything the rest of the package needs to know about
your raw ROXAS data: where the files live, how the images are organised
hierarchically, image EXIF properties, and the ROXAS (AI) settings used
during analysis. It is the required input for `collect_raw_data()` and
the `$images` component inside a `QWAmetadata` object.

The object carries a single attribute, `roxas_version` (`"roxas"` or
`"roxas_ai"`), which records which software produced the data and
determines the expected column set.

---

## Building a QWAimages object

In normal use, you do not call `QWAimages()` directly. Instead, you use
`build_QWAimages()`, which combines the output of
`extract_data_structure()` (the hierarchical labels) with
`collect_settings_data()` (the per-image ROXAS settings and EXIF
metadata). See the main `rxs2tria` vignette for a step-by-step walkthrough.

```{r build}
files        <- get_roxas_files("path/to/ROXAS_data", roxas_version = "roxas")
df_structure <- extract_data_structure(files, pattern = "...")
df_settings  <- collect_settings_data(df_structure)

rxs_images <- build_QWAimages(df_structure, df_settings)
```

`build_QWAimages()` checks the label hierarchy (aborting if it is
invalid), aligns the columns and types to the JSON schema for the
software version (adding missing required columns as `NA`, dropping
unrecognised columns, warning on coercions) and validates the result
against the schema (warnings only).

If you already have a data frame with the right columns — for example
after reading from a non-standard source — you can pass it directly to
`QWAimages()`. It infers or validates `roxas_version` from the
`$software` column and does the same alignment, but only warns on an
invalid hierarchy:

```{r construct-direct}
rxs_images <- QWAimages(my_df, roxas_version = "roxas")
```

---

## What the object contains

```{r inspect}
rxs_images          # same as print(rxs_images): prints the tibble
summary(rxs_images) # compact overview
```

`summary()` reports the software version, the count of images, slides,
woodpieces, and trees, the sites and species present, and the range of
`outmost_year` values.

The columns fall into the following groups:

**Hierarchical labels** — uniquely identify each image within the
sampling design and link images to the metadata tables in `QWAmetadata`:

| Column | Description |
|---|---|
| `site_label` | Site identifier |
| `tree_label` | Tree identifier (includes site) |
| `woodpiece_label` | Woodpiece identifier (includes tree) |
| `slide_label` | Slide identifier (includes woodpiece) |
| `image_label` | Image identifier (includes slide); used as the join key in `QWAdata` |
| `species_code` | Species code |

**File paths** — used by `collect_raw_data()` and `update_QWAdata()` to
locate the ROXAS output files:

| Column | Description |
|---|---|
| `fname_image` | Path to the image file |
| `fname_cells` | Path to the cells output file |
| `fname_rings` | Path to the rings output file |
| `fname_settings` | Path to the settings / metadata file |

File paths are part of submission files only; the `$images` of TRIA
dataset files have no `fname_*` columns.

**Image metadata** — properties extracted from the image EXIF data or
the ROXAS AI metadata file:

| Column | Description |
|---|---|
| `img_created_at` | Image capture timestamp |
| `img_width`, `img_height` | Image dimensions in pixels |
| `spatial_resolution` | Pixels per µm; required for the incomplete-innermost-ring check in `complete_QWAdata()` |
| `software` | Software that produced the data (`"roxas"` or `"roxas_ai"`); must match the `roxas_version` attribute |

**ROXAS settings** — parameters from the ROXAS settings or ROXAS AI
metadata file (e.g. magnification, threshold values). The exact columns
differ between `roxas_version` values.

**Dating** — `outmost_year` is the calendar year of the outermost
complete ring in the image, used to validate that ring years do not
exceed it.

**App inputs** — `only_ew` and `img_comment` (`colType` `meta_input`,
filled in the metadata app) and `comment_handled` (`colType` `qc_input`,
set in the flags app).

Optional columns (those not always present in ROXAS output) are `NA`
until populated. `complete_QWAimages()` adds all missing optional columns
except `qc_input` columns (`comment_handled`), initialised to `NA`.

---

## The `roxas_version` attribute and the `$software` column

`roxas_version` is stored both as the object attribute (the authoritative
source) and as the `$software` column (a per-row record). The two must
agree: `QWAimages()` sets `$software` to the resolved `roxas_version`
(with a warning if values changed), and all functions taking a `QWAimages`
object abort if they disagree:

```{r version-mismatch, eval = FALSE}
# Error if the attribute and the $software column disagree, e.g. after
# editing $software by hand:
#   x <QWAimages>: software must be "roxas" (the roxas_version attribute) in all rows.
#   i Rebuild the object with QWAimages().
```

The `$software` column is used to re-derive `roxas_version` when reading
from file (since attributes are not persisted in CSV).

---

## Checking a QWAimages object

```{r check}
check_QWAimages(rxs_images)
```

`check_QWAimages()` returns `TRUE` invisibly if no issue was found, `FALSE`
otherwise. With `strict = TRUE`, it aborts on the first issue instead of
warning. It is also run by `check_QWAmetadata()`.

- **Errors**: invalid object, i.e. structure labels missing or `NA`,
  duplicate `image_label`s, or `$software` not matching the
  `roxas_version` attribute.
- **Warnings**: values violating the schema of the stage
  (`submission = TRUE` for submission files, `FALSE` for TRIA dataset
  files; set by `check_QWAmetadata()`); labels not starting with their
  parent label, or a label in more than one parent; `outmost_year` in the
  future; missing `spatial_resolution`.
- **Information**: missing optional columns (except `qc_input` ones; add
  them with `complete_QWAimages()`) and empty values.

---

## Adding optional columns

```{r complete}
rxs_images_full <- complete_QWAimages(rxs_images)
```

Returns a new `QWAimages` object with all optional columns except
`qc_input` ones added and initialised to `NA`. Existing values are
preserved. `complete_QWAmetadata()` does this for `$images`.

---

## Persisting to disk

```{r write-read}
write_QWAimages(rxs_images, "output/my_dataset_QWAimages.csv.gz")

rxs_images <- read_QWAimages("output/my_dataset_QWAimages.csv.gz")
```

`write_QWAimages()` saves the tibble as a (optionally compressed) CSV.
The `roxas_version` attribute is **not** written to the file — it is
re-derived from the `$software` column when the file is read back by
`read_QWAimages()`. This means the `$software` column must be intact and
consistent for round-tripping to work correctly.

The `compress` argument adds a `.gz` extension if not already present.
Alternatively, naming the file with a `.csv.gz` extension is sufficient
— `vroom` compresses automatically.

Empty values are written as empty fields. With `drop_empty = TRUE`
(default), optional `meta_input`/`qc_input` columns (`only_ew`,
`img_comment`, `comment_handled`) that are empty in all rows are not
written. `read_QWAimages()` does not re-create them; use
`complete_QWAimages()`.
